region_chill_delivered_provenance.utah_d: utah_dixie (St. George / Washington County z8 core, St. George station ~2,624 ft): no USU-published numeric chill-hour accumulation figure for St. George or Washington County was found despite a targeted 2026-07-22 search (USU How to Grow Peaches, How to Grow Apples, the Washington County Fruits page, and the Utah Climate Center / peach chill pages give only per-variety chill REQUIREMENTS, never a regional accumulation total). This band is therefore elevation-bracketed INFERENCE, not a measured figure: St. George's ~2,624 ft sits between the two existing z8/z9 desert regions that bracket it, low_desert_az (Phoenix, ~1,100 ft, [100,400]) below and warm_arid (Las Cruces, ~3,900 ft, [450,850]) above, and Washington County Extension's own elevation-based fruit recommendation (apple and pear recommended only at the county's higher-elevation towns above ~5,300 ft, not the St. George core) places St. George nearer the Phoenix / marginal end, hence [250,450].
